forecasts.question: Will any Iranian ballistic missile or drone attack on a host-country target (Jordan, Bahrain, or Iraq) be confirmed by CENTCOM or UKMTO before EOD 2026-09-22?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 72h military activity forecast. A 9-day pause in Iranian ballistic missile and drone attacks on host-country targets held since the September 8–9 launch of 20 missiles at Jordan’s Muwaffaq Salti base (GlobalSecurity Day 203 update, September 18). Iran relayed conditions for ending the war via Doha on September 19 (Al Jazeera liveblog) and President Pezeshkian and FM Araghchi are confirmed for UNGA beginning September 22, creating short-term diplomatic incentives for restraint. IRGC naval harassment of commercial shipping at Hormuz continued (Trend tanker struck approximately September 18, Al Jazeera), but that event falls below the threshold of a host-country ballistic or drone attack. Base rate of fire-pause break within 72h during an active UNGA week with Doha channel open: 25%.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if CENTCOM (official press release or verified social media post) or UKMTO (security incident report) confirms a new Iranian ballistic missile or drone attack targeting US, coalition, or Gulf partner positions in Jordan, Bahrain, or Iraq, launched after EOD September 20, 2026, and before EOD September 22, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: CENTCOM official press release OR UKMTO incident report OR a TIER1 source (Reuters/AP/AFP) citing named US or coalition military officials confirming the attack origin as Iranian state forces.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Houthi attacks are not Iranian state military attacks and do NOT count toward YES. An attack with unattributed origin = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Iranian strikes inside Iranian territory or against Israeli territory = not a host-country target for this forecast; AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. Only Jordan, Bahrain, or Iraq targeting by confirmed Iranian state forces counts.

indicators.expected_effect: +70pp toward YES if observed before EOD Sep 22

forecasts.question: Will a held bilateral or proximity meeting between named Iranian and US senior officials (ministerial level or designated envoys) be confirmed at or on the sidelines of UNGA 2026 before EOD 2026-09-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: New 7-day diplomatic forecast. The US approved visas for Iran’s core delegation on September 17, including FM Araghchi and President Pezeshkian, for UNGA’s high-level debate opening September 22 (Al Jazeera, September 17). Iran relayed conditions for ending the war via the Doha channel on September 19 through Mohsen Rezaei (Al Jazeera liveblog). Trump described UNGA plans as centering on Iran and said ‘anything could happen.’ Iran’s official framing of UNGA attendance as a ‘legal right’ (IANS, September 20) is resistance posture, not conciliatory language, and FM Araghchi’s August 19 statement rejecting ceasefire remains the public record (Middle East Monitor). Devil’s Advocate correctly identified Rezaei as a hardline channel and cautioned against over-reading the diplomatic signal; Judge reduced from 0.35 to 0.33. P=0.33 reflects meaningful but fragile diplomatic momentum.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a TIER1 source reports a held, face-to-face or formally convened bilateral or proximity meeting between named senior Iranian officials (FM Araghchi, President Pezeshkian, or a designated Iranian envoy) and named senior US officials (Secretary of State Rubio, National Security Advisor, or designated US envoy), whether direct or mediated by a named third party, at any UNGA-related venue in New York or a named city, before EOD September 27, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Two independent TIER1 sources (Reuters/AP/AFP/Al Jazeera/Bloomberg) OR one TIER1 source plus an official readout from Iran MFA, US State Department, or a named mediator (Oman/Qatar/Pakistan).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: An informal hallway encounter without seated agenda and no official readout = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A phone call or written message relay without a held session = AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO. A multilateral UNSC meeting where both Iran and the US participate does not constitute a bilateral meeting; AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO unless a separate bilateral session is separately confirmed.

forecasts.question: Will commercial shipping through the Strait of Hormuz reach >=30 vessels/day (7-day rolling average) before EOD 2026-10-03?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Hormuz commercial traffic remained at 7–14 vessels per day through September 18, 2026 (GlobalSecurity Day 203 update; straits.live Day 203 tracker), against the 30/day threshold (7-day rolling average) and far below the pre-war 85/day baseline. The 10-day average stood at approximately 13 transits per day as of September 9–13. Iran’s IRGC navy struck the Togo-flagged tanker Trend for unauthorized passage approximately September 18 (Al Jazeera liveblog), demonstrating continued active enforcement of the blockade. Insurance war-risk cover remains prohibitive; no named insurer has announced reinstatement for Hormuz passage. With 13 days remaining to the October 3 horizon and no ceasefire, no Iranian naval-halt signal, and active tanker strikes ongoing, the probability of a sustained 30/day traffic average is revised sharply downward to 0.07.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if any AIS-based ship-tracking source (IMF PortWatch, Straits.live, MarineTraffic, Lloyd’s List Intelligence) records >=30 commercial transits/day as a 7-day rolling average at any point between 2026-09-03 and 2026-10-03.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: AIS-based tracker + one TIER1 or OSINT confirmation (Bloomberg/Reuters/Lloyd’s List).
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: Naval escort vessels and warships do not count toward commercial transit; if trackers diverge by >20%, flag AMBIGUOUS.

forecasts.question: Will Likud win the most Knesset seats (seat plurality) in the October 27, 2026 Israeli election?
forecasts.delta_reason: UPDATE. Five polls published after Knesset candidate lists closed show Yashar (Eisenkot) averaging 22.2 seats against Likud’s 21.2, with Yashar leading in four of the five surveys (Jerusalem Post). Haaretz published a September 17 poll showing Likud’s seat count dropping while the pro-Netanyahu bloc narrowly edged ahead at bloc level. An outlier i24NEWS poll (September 9) showed Likud at 27 seats against Yashar’s 22; no subsequent poll has replicated that result. P=0.37 (was 0.42) reflects the consistent polling trend showing Yashar at or above Likud in seat plurality, though the race remains within normal polling error at 37 days from election.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if official Knesset election results published by the Israeli Central Elections Committee show Likud winning more seats than any other single party in the October 27, 2026 election.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Israeli Central Elections Committee official results, carried by Times of Israel/Haaretz/Reuters/AP.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If Likud and one other party tie on seats: AMBIGUOUS-RESOLVE-AS-NO (no plurality). Exit polls alone do not resolve; official preliminary results suffice if published before EOD Oct 27.

indicators.name: Polls showing Likud >=23 seats, ahead of Yashar

forecasts.question: Will Netanyahu’s coalition lose its Knesset majority or dissolve early before 2026-10-27?
forecasts.delta_reason: No material movement. Saturday cadence; F7 reviewed Sundays only per ambiguity rule. Knesset dissolved July 17, 2026 (natural end of 4-year term, first since 1988, per Times of Israel/Al Jazeera). Both resolution paths are operationally moot: ‘dissolve early’ = NO (full term completed); ‘lose majority’ = NO (one-seat majority of 61/120 held through natural dissolution). Remaining YES path requires extraordinary post-dissolution parliamentary reconstitution before October 27 — negligible probability given the October 27 election is 37 days away. Next formal Sunday review: September 21, 2026.
forecasts.resolution_criteria: YES if a Knesset roll-call vote confirms coalition loss of majority (61 seats), OR if Netanyahu announces early dissolution and election date moves earlier than 2026-10-27. NO if coalition survives to mandatory election date with 61+ seats intact.
forecasts.resolution_source_rule: Knesset official record + Reuters/Haaretz/Times of Israel. Polling alone does not resolve.
forecasts.ambiguity_rule: If coalition drops below 61 but Netanyahu remains caretaker PM until election: YES. If a single party departs but coalition retains 61+: NO. Reviewed weekly only (Sundays); no intra-week deltas.
